Subject: Strata AI - Dedicated GPU pool orchestration & activation checklist

Hi Claire / Strata team —

Thanks again for the commitment. Attached is the activation checklist and the current SOW (v1.2) for the Dedicated GPU pool. High-level plan we propose:

- Primary region: us-west-2 (avoid your existing East latency for west-coast users)
- Fallback region: us-east-1 for burst / DR
- Initial pool: 50 x H100-80GB-equivalent instances (we can scope mix of A100/H100 based on pricing)
- Autoscaling policy (proposed): min 6 nodes / max 120 nodes, scale step 10 nodes, cooldown 120s, burst cap to cross-region when utilization > 85%
- KV/prefix caching: enabled with 24h TTL on inference front-door
- Data isolation: dedicated VPC peering and customer-kept audit logs (SOC2 evidence attached on request)

Immediate asks from our side to keep timeline moving (target activation window: Nov 16–19):
1) Confirm preferred primary region (US-W vs US-E) and whether cross-region bursting is allowed in your procurement terms.
2) Procurement: please review the SOW and confirm DocuSign recipient for signature.
3) Security: please share SOC2 scope contact if you need any additional artifacts beyond what we sent last week.
4) Tech: please confirm expected p95 latency SLO and average request length (tokens per request) — we used 512 tokens as planning baseline.

Attachments: strata_activation_checklist.xlsx (activation checklist), sow-dedicated-v1.2.pdf (SOW)

Next step: Ben will propose 3 times for a 60-min technical kickoff where we walk infra, autoscale rules, and rollback policies.

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0134

Monica / Jordan —

Confirming infra side notes based on the 350-token average:
- Warm floor: we can maintain 6 warm GPUs with prefix KV caching; estimated incremental cost ~18% over strictly zero-warm baseline (rough estimate; will provide detailed cost matrix).
- Thrashing: step=10 nodes & cooldown=120s is reasonable; we prefer a staged policy for the first 72 hours after launch (step 6 / cooldown 90s) to avoid overshoot during traffic discovery.
- Cross-region KV replication: eventual consistency model; typical convergence 20–90s for small hot-prefixes when using async replication across us-west-2 <-> us-east-1. Stateful session failover will require short-time rewarm for sessions; recommend short sticky routing TTL (30s) in front-door to reduce cross-region replays.

Action items I will deliver by EOD Wed Nov 4:
- Detailed cost delta table for warm floor vs zero-warm for 50/100/200 GPU pool sizes
- Proposed ramp policy YAML we can deploy as part of activation runbook

Rishi
Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
